cases.title: Outbound Busy Signal Investigation — Ringba
cases.findings: Outbound calls getting busy signal; client's call center says calls never reached them. SIP analysis of 5 call legs shows: initial carrier gateway 503 errors, then 603 Decline from far end, then eventual success on final attempt. The 'busy' = destination actively declining (603 Decline). Carrier gateways returning 503 on initial attempts also concerning. Client uses sequential dialing (tries multiple targets).
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted SIP analysis. 5 UUIDs analyzed. Key finding: 603 Decline from far end = destination rejecting, not network issue. 503 from carrier gateways on initial attempts = pre-routing rejection. Call center may have PBX auto-reject or queue capacity limits.
cases.response: SIP analysis shared — recommend client check PBX/ACD auto-reject rules and queue capacity.

cases.title: No Routes Found PE2 — Ringba (Alaska PPT Filtering)
cases.findings: Root cause: Profit Protection Threshold (PPT) filtering blocks Alaska (+19076005911) routes. Customer tariff $0.0035/min, PPT $0.10/min. Available carriers at $0.04/min and $0.225/min — both blocked by PPT. no_routes_found_with_ppt=true confirmed in TREAT routing response. Initial CDR analysis incorrectly identified missing outbound profile — CORRECTED after TREAT showed PPT is the actual issue. Call Control/TeXML transfers route through app layer, not via assigned outbound profile.
cases.notes: Sensei-assisted deep analysis. TREAT confirmed PPT root cause on 3/5 samples (2 timed out, re-queried). Key lesson: don't rely on CDR outbound_profile_id=null for Call Control transfers — verify routing response data. Drafted customer response (pending Sean approval): offer PPT adjustment or custom Alaska rate escalation.
cases.response: Drafted — awaiting Sean approval to send. Options: (1) adjust PPT with cost acceptance, (2) escalate to billing for custom Alaska rate.
